_comment: Curated gap-fill data NOT present in AAindex. ALL values below are FACT-CHECKED against the cited sources (fetched and verified 2026-07), not from memory. Full attribution in SOURCES.md (this skill's directory, section 'Curated gap-fill'). pKa: IMGT (Asp/Glu/Lys/Arg/His) + Wikipedia (Cys/Tyr). H-bond donor/acceptor counts: IMGT Table 3 (atom counts). Net side-chain charge: consistent with AAindex1 KLEP840101 (Klein, Kanehisa & DeLisi 1984; PMID 6547351).

pka_sidechain._source: FACT-CHECKED. IMGT (https://www.imgt.org/IMGTeducation/Aide-memoire/_UK/aminoacids/charge/index.html): Asp 3.9, Glu 4.2, Lys 10.5, Arg 12.5, His 6.0. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cysteine): Cys thiol 8.33. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amino_acid): Tyr phenolic ~10. null = no ionizable side chain.

pka_notes.R: Guanidinium, effectively always protonated (+1) at physiological pH; pKa shifts are rare.
pka_notes.K: Primary amine, +1 at physiological pH; slightly weaker base than Arg.
pka_notes.H: Imidazole, pKa near physiological pH -> protonation state is pH-sensitive; the classic 'switchable' charge. ~10% protonated at pH 7 (Wikipedia).
pka_notes.C: Thiol, neutral at physiological pH; can be deprotonated (thiolate) in specific active-site environments (e.g., cysteine proteases).
pka_notes.Y: Phenol, neutral at physiological pH; weak acid.
pka_notes._nulls: The 13 null residues are NOT ionized at physiological pH (so null is functionally correct for charge reasoning). Two sub-cases: (a) 9 are truly non-ionizable - no acidic/basic side-chain proton at all: A, G, V, L, I, M, F, W, P. (b) 4 are weakly acidic at very high pKa (~13-15) and thus uncharged at physiological pH: S, T (hydroxyl) and N, Q (amide). They are polar but uncharged.
pka_notes._caveat: In proteins these values shift substantially (especially His, Cys, Asp, Glu) depending on local environment. Discussed in Stryer (2015) and Lehninger et al. (2017).

hbond_donors._source: FACT-CHECKED. IMGT Table 3 (https://www.imgt.org/IMGTeducation/Aide-memoire/_UK/aminoacids/charge/index.html): number of hydrogen-bond DONOR ATOMS in the side chain. (Alternative capacity-based count: AAindex1 FAUJ880109, Fauchere et al. 1988, PMID 3209351, gives R=4, K=2, etc.)

hbond_acceptors._source: FACT-CHECKED. IMGT Table 3 (https://www.imgt.org/IMGTeducation/Aide-memoire/_UK/aminoacids/charge/index.html): number of hydrogen-bond ACCEPTOR ATOMS in the side chain. Note: counts are protonation-state dependent; e.g. protonated Arg/Lys are poor acceptors (0).

hbond_notes.R: Guanidinium: 3 N-H donor atoms (NE, NH1, NH2) + planar bidentate geometry; the amine N is a very weak acceptor (counted 0 when protonated). Forms strong, directionally flexible salt bridges/H-bonds with carboxylates, phosphates, and carbonyls.
hbond_notes.K: Primary amine: 1 donor atom (NZ, up to 3 N-H), single-directional; salt bridges are weaker and less geometrically flexible than Arg's.
hbond_notes.H: Imidazole: 2 donor/acceptor atoms (ND1, NE2) when neutral; loses acceptor character when protonated (donor only).
hbond_notes.D: Carboxylate: 2 acceptor atoms (OD1, OD2), 1 donor; bidentate binding to cations.

partial_charge_sidechain._source: Net side-chain charge at pH 7.4. Consistent with AAindex1 entry KLEP840101 (Klein, P., Kanehisa, M. and DeLisi, C. 1984; PMID 6547351) and IMGT (5 charged side chains at pH 7: D, E negative; K, R, H positive). His counted as 0 here (mixture of ~10% protonated at pH 7 per Wikipedia; use pka_sidechain for context).
